name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
summary: A curl performed on an incline bench so the arms start behind the torso, stretching the long head of the biceps. Use lighter weights than standing curls.
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about 45-60 degrees and sit back with your head, shoulders and hips against the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and let the arms hang straight down, palms facing forward.
Plant your feet and keep the shoulder blades pressed lightly into the bench.
execution: Curl both dumbbells upward by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms pointing down.
Squeeze at the top without letting the elbows move forward.
Lower slowly to a full stretch with the arms hanging.
Repeat for all reps without lifting the back from the bench.
cues: Let the arms hang behind the body
mistakes: Letting the elbows swing forward: keep the upper arms vertical so the stretch stays on the biceps.
Using too heavy a load and jerking the weights: choose a lighter pair and go slowly.
Lifting the shoulders off the pad: keep the back in contact with the bench.
Dropping the weights quickly from the top: control the lowering to protect the elbow and shoulder.
